newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore dollar hits new 30-month low.
newsitem.headline: Singapore dollar hits new 30-month low.

text.p: The Singapore dollar slumped to a new 30-month low of 1.4603 against the U.S. dollar in Friday morning trade in line with continuing weakness in regional currencies, forex dealers said.
At 0304 GMT, the Singapore dollar was quoted at 1.4600/10 to the U.S. unit against a morning high of 1.4550/60.
"I think U.S. funds are behind the dollar buying. They're still very short (dollars)," a European bank dealer said.
She said the rise in dollar/Sing had been triggered by gains in the dollar/ringgit, which touched a high of 2.60.
"I would buy the dollar/Sing on dips to see 1.47 in the near term," she added.
Dealers said the domestic currency was being pressured by weakness in other Southeast Asian currencies, which have come under heavy speculative attack in recent weeks.
